terms.comment: A country takes a preposition: in Finlandiam (to), in Finlandiā (in), ē Finlandiā (from).
From the Fennī, a northern people in Tacitus (Tac. G. 46, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Finnland: Finnia

sources: Lewis & Short: Fenni
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus (Dresden, 1861), German–Latin index, read in the scan at archive.org (the 1909 edition at columbia.edu could not be reached page by page); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
